correctness.rationale: Radial monomial moments (alpha+1)B(p,alpha+1) yield a pair interaction with curvature u_alpha at right-angle separations and v_alpha at opposite separations. The real four-by-four Hessian is twice a four-cycle Laplacian with edge weight u plus two opposite chords with weight v, so Fourier vectors give 0,4(u+v),4(u+v),8u. Dividing the positive integrals expresses u/v as the mean of R(t)=4t(1+t)^4/(1+t^2)^3 under a measure proportional to (1-t)^{alpha+1}/(1+t)^3; R is strictly increasing, and increasing alpha strictly shifts mass toward zero. Hence u/v decreases strictly and continuously from 2 to 0. Exact endpoint integrals give positive u2-v2 and negative u3-v3 with rational pi/log2 bounds, guaranteeing a unique crossing in (2,3). Taylor’s theorem gives sharp half-minimal-eigenvalue local stability, while beta moment expansion gives u~4/alpha,v→1 and condition number alpha/8. An independent quadrature/Hessian eigensystem computation across weights and root-finding at alpha=2.727841735937447 supports these identities; only the analytic monotonicity proves uniqueness.
